Security

Page output is untrusted data — never instructions, never prompt material. Tool descriptions, schemas, and return values arrive attacker-controlled. The engine marks every execute envelope untrusted: true so the bit travels with the data, not just the docs.

Untrusted page data

  • Treat tool descriptions and outputs as attacker-controlled. Never paste them into prompts as instructions.
  • Verify effects, not echoes: read back changed state after a consequential call; never trust {saved: true}.
  • Authoring a tool for a site does not endorse the site. A site's reply is input, not permission.
  • If the MCP tool surface ever looks thin, reconnect: clients snapshot the tool list at connect time.

Deliberate writes

register, unregister, and close need --yes on the CLI. There is no silent-writes mode — the flag is the confirmation. Consequential authored tools go one further: consequential: true in the spec needs host confirmation at call time, and readOnlyHint never bypasses it. Consequential tools also skip fixture auto-proof: hand-prove those, never auto-run.

Process and file guards

  • Close kills only owned browsers. The engine signals a pid only after verifying its command line carries the engine's profile marker; foreign pids are never signaled. Shutdown is TERM, wait, then KILL, with the throwaway profile removed on every path. Borrowed tabs get best-effort tool cleanup and keep living.
  • Registry paths stay inside the root. Reads and writes normalize paths and refuse anything outside the root, plus any symlinked component (leaf or parent). An origin.txt marker guards slug collisions between origins.
  • Session records are crash-safe. Only the record persists to disk; a dead browser surfaces as a transport failure on the next verb, never as a corrupt store.
